close_reason: Landed in c430f73 (paired with .5). Decision record now lives in two places: (1) inline comment block above the PartialEq impls in digest.rs, (2) PLAN.md 'Sibling-of-Id newtype, fallible construction only' section. Both cite: Id's SAFE-CHAR set is open (RFC 8620 §1.2) and admits opaque From<String>; Sha256's ABNF is closed (draft-atwood-jmap-cid-00 §2, exactly 64 lowercase hex chars) and demands strictly fallible construction.
description: DEFEND ON REVIEW: jmap-types::Id implements infallible From<String> and From<&str> (crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs macro at line 72), treating the value as opaque per RFC 8620 §1.2. jmap-cid-types::Sha256 deliberately does NOT — only TryFrom<String>, TryFrom<&str>, FromStr (all fallible) are provided. The asymmetry is correct because draft-atwood-jmap-cid-00 §2 defines sha256-value with a tight ABNF () — exactly 64 lowercase hex chars, not opaque. Allowing infallible construction would let arbitrary garbage round-trip through serialize and emerge as a malformed wire field. A future contributor who reads jmap-types::Id and proposes 'add From<String> to Sha256 for consistency with sibling newtypes' should be told: Id's character set is open (URL-safe base64 alphabet, server-assigned, no client-side parse rule), Sha256's is closed (ABNF fixed-length lowercase hex, both sides validate). The TryFrom-only construction is the right shape. Keep this decision.
title: Sha256 deliberately rejects infallible From<String>/From<&str> vs sibling Id newtype — defend this asymmetry
